title: What If Everyone on Earth Had Air Conditioning?

scenes.text: What if every home on Earth had air conditioning? Today, almost nobody in the hottest places does.
Of 2.8 billion people in the world's hottest regions, only 8 percent have it.
In the United States and Japan, more than 90 percent of homes do.
The world already runs about 1.6 billion air conditioners. Cooling uses around 10 percent of all electricity.
The International Energy Agency expects 5.6 billion units by 2050, and cooling demand to triple.
In India, cooling could grow from 10 percent of peak power demand to 45 percent. Comfort for billions comes with a bill.
